laws.title: Drunk Driving — Near Zero Tolerance, Passengers Liable
laws.subtitle: Road Traffic Law — .03% BAC; passengers can be prosecuted
laws.fullDescription: Japan's legal limit is 0.03% BAC (lower than most countries). Uniquely, passengers who knowingly allow a drunk driver, and those who provided the alcohol, can also be prosecuted.
laws.penalty: Driver: up to 5 years + ¥1 million fine. Passenger who allowed drunk driver: up to 3 years + ¥500,000.
exceptions: None

quiz.q: In Japan, besides the drunk driver, who can be prosecuted?
options: Passengers who allowed the driver to drive drunk
quiz.explanation: Japan holds passengers who allowed a drunk driver, and those who provided the alcohol, criminally liable.

laws.title: Japanese Etiquette — Bowing and Business Card Ritual
laws.subtitle: Bow depth = respect level; never write on a business card
laws.fullDescription: Bowing (お辞儀, ojigi): 15° casual, 30° formal, 45° deep apology. Business cards (名刺, meishi): exchange with both hands and slight bow, study it briefly, never write on it or put it in your back pocket. On trains: phones on silent, no calls. Slurping noodles is acceptable. Say 'Itadakimasu' before eating.
laws.penalty: Not legal — improper business card etiquette can cause serious professional offence.
exceptions: Handshakes accepted with foreigners
International business contexts are more flexible

quiz.q: What should you NEVER do with a Japanese business card?
quiz.explanation: Writing on a Japanese business card is considered highly disrespectful — treat it as an extension of the person.

laws.title: Bicycle Helmet Law 2023 — Strongly Encouraged
laws.subtitle: Road Traffic Law revision Apr 2023 — Advisory for all ages
laws.fullDescription: From April 2023, all bicycle riders in Japan are 'encouraged' to wear helmets under a revised Road Traffic Law — mandatory for children, strongly advisory for adults. Japan previously had very low helmet rates; the 2023 update responds to rising cycling fatalities.
laws.penalty: No fine for adult non-compliance currently — but police can issue guidance. Child helmet rules enforced by parents.
exceptions: Children under school age: parents responsible
Professional racing helmets already standard

quiz.q: When did Japan update its bicycle helmet law?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Road Traffic Law was revised in April 2023 to strongly encourage all cyclists to wear helmets.

laws.title: Drug Laws — Extremely Strict; Cannabis Illegal
laws.subtitle: Narcotics Control Law — Even prescription drugs can be banned
laws.fullDescription: Japan has some of the world's strictest drug laws. Cannabis is fully illegal (unlike many Western countries), and possession carries up to 5 years imprisonment. Even some common Western medications (pseudoephedrine, some ADHD drugs like Adderall) are controlled substances. Travelers must obtain advance permission (Yunyu Kakunin-sho) for controlled medications.
laws.penalty: Cannabis possession: up to 5 years. Stimulants (methamphetamine): up to 10 years. Customs officials inspect medications.
exceptions: Licensed medical practitioners
Pre-authorised imported medicines with proper paperwork
laws.sourceLabel: Narcotics and Psychotropics Control Law — Japan

quiz.q: What common Western medication requires special import permission to bring to Japan?
quiz.explanation: Many ADHD medications containing amphetamines (like Adderall) are controlled stimulants in Japan and require advance import permission.

laws.title: Train & Public Transport Etiquette
laws.subtitle: Priority seating; phone calls prohibited on trains
laws.fullDescription: Japan's train etiquette is among the strictest in the world. No phone calls on trains (set to silent/manner mode). Priority seats for elderly, disabled, pregnant passengers — healthy commuters should not occupy them. Large bags must be held in front or stored overhead. Eating on local trains is considered rude (Shinkansen exception). Boarding only after passengers exit.
laws.penalty: Not legally enforceable — but public disapproval (kuuki wo yomu — 'reading the air') is intense.
exceptions: Shinkansen (bullet trains) allow eating and more relaxed rules
Tourist-heavy routes often more lenient

quiz.q: What is strictly prohibited on Japanese local trains?
quiz.explanation: Phone calls on Japanese local trains are considered very rude — phones must be in 'manner mode' (silent).

laws.title: Knife & Sword Control Law — Blades Over 6cm Illegal to Carry
laws.subtitle: Firearms and Swords Control Law — samurai swords require registration
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Firearms and Swords Control Law (銃砲刀剣類所持等取締法) prohibits carrying any blade longer than 6cm in public without a legitimate reason. Samurai swords (nihonto) and other traditional blades are classified as 'swords' and require formal registration with the Board of Education. Japan has some of the lowest knife-crime rates in the world partly as a result of these strict controls. Even pocket knives carried 'just in case' can result in arrest if police deem there is no reasonable purpose.
laws.penalty: Carrying a blade over 6cm: up to 2 years imprisonment or fine up to ¥300,000. Unregistered sword possession: up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥500,000 fine.
exceptions: Culinary professionals carrying kitchen knives to/from work with reasonable cause
Hunters and fishermen with licensed equipment in appropriate context
laws.sourceLabel: Firearms and Swords Control Law — e-Gov Japan

quiz.q: What is the blade length limit for carrying a knife in public in Japan?
quiz.explanation: Under Japan's Firearms and Swords Control Law, carrying any blade longer than 6cm in public without legitimate reason is illegal and can result in up to 2 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Pet Import Quarantine — 180-Day Microchip Wait or 180 Days Quarantine
laws.subtitle: Rabies Prevention Law — Import of dogs and cats requires strict pre-arrival compliance
laws.fullDescription: Japan is rabies-free and enforces some of the toughest pet import rules on earth. To bring a dog or cat into Japan, the animal must be microchipped, vaccinated against rabies twice (at least 30 days apart), and have a blood titre test showing antibodies ≥ 0.5 IU/ml drawn at an MAFF-approved laboratory. After the titre, the pet must wait at least 180 days before entering Japan. Advance notification (at least 40 days before arrival) is mandatory to the Animal Quarantine Service at the destination airport. Pets that do not meet every requirement face up to 180 days of quarantine in Japan at the owner’s expense. Pets arriving from designated rabies-free regions (Hawaii, Guam, Iceland, Australia, NZ, UK, Ireland, several others) follow a slightly shorter pathway but microchipping and prior vaccination remain mandatory.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant pet: up to 180 days mandatory quarantine at owner’s expense (¥3,000-¥3,500 per day). Falsifying documents: up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine under the Rabies Prevention Law.
exceptions: Assistance dogs accompanying people with disabilities follow a dedicated fast-track but still require the 180-day wait period
Pets in direct transit (not leaving the international zone) do not require full import procedures
laws.sourceLabel: Rabies Prevention Law — Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries

quiz.q: How long must a dog or cat wait after its rabies blood titre test before entering Japan without quarantine?
quiz.explanation: Japan requires a minimum 180-day wait between the rabies antibody titre blood draw and arrival — otherwise the pet faces up to 180 days quarantine on arrival at the owner’s expense.

laws.title: Stimulant Medication Import Ban — Adderall, Vyvanse, Codeine Tightly Controlled
laws.subtitle: Stimulants Control Act + Narcotics Control Act — Even prescribed ADHD drugs banned
laws.fullDescription: Japan’s Stimulants Control Act (Kakuseizai Torishimari Hō) prohibits the importation of amphetamines and methamphetamines without exception. Critically, this includes prescription ADHD medications that are routine elsewhere: Adderall (dextroamphetamine + amphetamine), Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine), Dexedrine, and certain forms of methylphenidate. Even a US-written prescription is not a legal defence; the drug itself is banned. Codeine-containing products over 10 percent require specific approval. For other prescription medications (including methylphenidate-based Ritalin/Concerta in limited circumstances, certain narcotic painkillers, and some psychiatric medications) travellers must apply for a Yakkan Shoumei (import certificate) from the prefectural Narcotic Control Officer at least 2–4 weeks before travel. Possession of banned stimulants at Narita or Haneda has resulted in the detention and deportation of multiple Western tourists, including several high-profile cases.
laws.penalty: Import of banned stimulants (Adderall, Vyvanse): up to 10 years imprisonment + large fines under Stimulants Control Act. Import of controlled narcotics without Yakkan Shoumei: confiscation + deportation + potential prosecution.
exceptions: Medications for which a valid Yakkan Shoumei has been obtained in advance from the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
Under-the-counter permitted brands (Strattera, Concerta in limited form) with documentation
laws.sourceLabel: Stimulants Control Act — Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare

quiz.q: Can a traveller bring Adderall into Japan with a valid US prescription?
options: Yes, but only for a 30-day supply
No — Adderall contains amphetamine which is banned under the Stimulants Control Act
quiz.explanation: Adderall contains amphetamine, which is flat-out banned under Japan’s Stimulants Control Act. A foreign prescription is not a defence; possession at the airport has led to detention and deportation.

laws.title: Tattoo Rules at Onsen and Public Baths — Historical Yakuza Association
laws.subtitle: Operator discretion — Many onsen, pools, gyms and beaches still refuse entry to tattooed patrons
laws.fullDescription: Tattoos in Japan carry a cultural association with the yakuza (organised crime groups), and many traditional onsen (hot springs), sentō (public baths), gyms, swimming pools, and some beaches refuse entry to tattooed visitors. The rule is not national law but is enforced by operators under their private-premises rights and posted no-tattoo signage (入れ墨お断り/タトゥーお断り). Tokyo 2020 Olympic athletes drew public attention to the issue; since then a growing number of onsen in Hakone, Beppu, and Kusatsu accept tattooed guests, and ‘tattoo-friendly’ maps are published by tourism boards. Rental cover stickers (up to about 20 × 20 cm) can allow entry to some moderate-sized tattoos. Private baths (kashikiri-buro) inside ryokan are almost always tattoo-OK. Tattooed visitors should check in advance; showing up and being refused is common, and most operators will refund only if no service has been rendered.
laws.penalty: No legal penalty — refusal is at operator discretion under private-premises rights. Lawsuits challenging refusal have been uniformly unsuccessful, though Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare has since 2016 encouraged hospitality operators to relax rules for foreign visitors.
exceptions: Tattoo-friendly onsen publish their status on Japan Tourism Board maps
Private family baths and kashikiri-buro in ryokan typically accept tattooed guests
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Tourism Organization — Tattoo-Friendly Facilities Guide

quiz.q: Why do many Japanese onsen still refuse entry to tattooed visitors?
options: A national law banning public tattoos
Historical association of tattoos with yakuza organised crime
quiz.explanation: The refusal is not legal but cultural. Tattoos are historically associated with the yakuza in Japan; many onsen and public baths still refuse tattooed entrants under private-premises rules.

laws.title: Japan's Corporate Governance Reform — Stewardship Code and Cross-Shareholding
laws.subtitle: Japan forced corporations to improve governance; decades of cross-shareholding unwound since 2012
laws.fullDescription: Japan's 'lost decades' (1990s–2000s) were partly attributed to poor corporate governance: cross-shareholding (companies holding each other's shares to prevent takeovers), rubber-stamp boards, and prioritization of employees over shareholders. The Abenomics reforms (2012–2020) introduced the Japan Stewardship Code (2014) and Corporate Governance Code (2015) — institutional investors must vote shares actively, boards must include independent directors, and companies must explain why they hold unprofitable cross-shareholdings. The Tokyo Stock Exchange's 2023 'request' to companies with Price-to-Book ratios below 1.0 to outline improvement plans drove unprecedented share buybacks and corporate restructuring. Warren Buffett's large investments in Japanese trading companies in 2020 spotlighted the governance improvements. Japanese corporations are still unwinding cross-shareholding structures built over 60 years.
laws.penalty: Corporate governance code violations are 'comply or explain' (not criminal law). Companies that ignore TSE guidance: de-listing risk, investor pressure. Actual fraud: Financial Instruments and Exchange Act violations, up to 10 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Closely held family companies below public reporting thresholds
Strategic shareholdings with documented business purpose
Financial group holding structures

quiz.q: What term describes the practice of Japanese companies holding each other's shares to prevent hostile takeovers?
quiz.explanation: Cross-shareholding (持ち合い, mochiai) refers to the practice of Japanese companies holding each other's shares — historically used to build business relationships and prevent hostile takeovers. Abenomics reforms since 2012 pushed companies to unwind these holdings, improving capital efficiency and corporate governance.

laws.title: Japanese Food Safety Laws — Fugu (Puffer Fish) Licensing and Food Hygiene Act
laws.subtitle: Japan requires special licenses to prepare fugu; food safety laws are among world's strictest
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Food Sanitation Act (Shokuhin Eisei Hō) and prefectural regulations create one of the world's strictest food safety frameworks. The most famous example: fugu (puffer fish/Takifugu) contains tetrodotoxin — a neurotoxin with no antidote. Preparing fugu for sale requires a special prefecture-issued license obtained after 2–3 years of apprenticeship and a rigorous examination. Only licensed chefs may serve fugu. Approximately 30–40% of fugu-related deaths are self-prepared (unlicensed). The Osaka 2025 World Expo relaxed some fugu regulations for specific licensed venues. Japan also has the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP) system mandated for all food businesses since 2021. Japanese food labeling laws require disclosure of all 28 allergens, country of origin for fresh fish and meat, and specific claims about Japanese traditional ingredients.
laws.penalty: Serving fugu without license: criminal prosecution under Food Sanitation Act + license revocation of restaurant. HACCP violations: inspections + business suspension. False food labeling: up to 2 years imprisonment + fines.
exceptions: Personal consumption of self-caught fugu (not served to others)
Licensed fugu chefs working within their licensed establishment
Scientific research on tetrodotoxin at approved institutions
laws.sourceLabel: Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — Food Safety

quiz.q: Why does Japan require a special license to prepare fugu (puffer fish)?
options: Fugu is an endangered species requiring catch limit compliance
Fugu contains tetrodotoxin, a neurotoxin with no antidote that can be lethal if improperly prepared
Fugu preparation involves proprietary techniques protected as trade secrets
Fugu is a cultural heritage dish requiring certified traditional preparation
quiz.explanation: Fugu (puffer fish) contains tetrodotoxin — a neurotoxin 1,200 times more lethal than cyanide by mass, with no known antidote. Improperly prepared fugu can cause paralysis and death. Japan requires 2–3 years of apprenticeship and a prefecture examination to obtain a fugu preparation license, a system that has dramatically reduced but not eliminated fugu-related fatalities.

laws.title: Abe Assassination & State Funeral Controversy
laws.subtitle: Shinzo Abe's 2022 murder and his state funeral triggered Japan's worst political scandal in years
laws.fullDescription: Former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe was assassinated on July 8, 2022 — shot during a campaign speech in Nara — the first assassination of a Japanese leader in decades. His killer cited Abe's connections to the Unification Church (founded by Sun Myung Moon). Subsequent investigation revealed that hundreds of Liberal Democratic Party politicians had deep ties to the Unification Church, which prosecutors alleged engaged in predatory fundraising from Japanese families. PM Kishida's decision to hold an expensive state funeral (¥2.5 billion) without parliamentary approval proved deeply unpopular; his approval ratings collapsed, and he announced he would not seek re-election in 2024.
laws.penalty: No specific law was violated by the state funeral — no law required parliamentary approval. The LDP's Unification Church ties prompted a Religious Corporations Law review. Kishida ordered cabinet ministers to sever Church ties.
exceptions: State funerals require Cabinet decision but no parliamentary vote under current law
Donations to religious organizations are tax-deductible — the Church's fundraising used this provision
Victims of Unification Church donation solicitation can seek relief through courts
laws.sourceLabel: Japanese Cabinet Secretariat — State Funeral Implementation

quiz.q: What political scandal emerged from the investigation into Shinzo Abe's assassination?
options: LDP politicians were found to have hidden foreign donations
Hundreds of LDP politicians were revealed to have deep ties to the Unification Church
The assassin was found to be a foreign agent
Abe's security detail was found criminally negligent
quiz.explanation: Investigation into Abe's assassin's motive — grievance against the Unification Church — revealed that hundreds of LDP politicians had deep ties to the Church, triggering Japan's worst political scandal in years and collapsing PM Kishida's approval ratings.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Partnership Ordinances & Equality Debate
laws.subtitle: Japan is the only G7 country without same-sex partnership recognition at national level
laws.fullDescription: Japan remains the only G7 country without national same-sex partnership recognition, despite majority public support for equality. Over 330 municipalities had created local 'partnership certificates' by 2024 — non-binding declarations without legal force. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government launched its own partnership system in 2022. National legislative efforts stalled repeatedly; the ruling LDP is divided. In June 2023, the Promotion of Understanding of LGBTQ Individuals Act passed — a watered-down law that merely promotes 'understanding' without creating rights. Tokyo District Court (2024) ruled that the lack of same-sex marriage was unconstitutional; cases are pending at appellate level.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties for sexual orientation — Japan decriminalized homosexuality in 1880 under Meiji-era reform. Employment discrimination based on sexual orientation has limited legal recourse. Hate speech protections are weak.
exceptions: Municipal partnership certificates provide limited practical benefits at local government level
Some private companies recognize same-sex partnerships for employee benefits independently
Foreign same-sex spouses of Japanese citizens have limited visa recognition in some contexts
laws.sourceLabel: Japanese Ministry of Justice — LGBTQ Rights

quiz.q: Among G7 nations, what is Japan's unique status regarding same-sex partnerships?
options: Japan has the most permissive same-sex marriage law in Asia
Japan is the only G7 country without national same-sex partnership recognition
Japan was the first Asian country to legalize same-sex marriage
Japan requires same-sex couples to register in both their home countries
quiz.explanation: Japan is the only G7 country without national same-sex partnership recognition — despite majority public support for equality, over 330 municipalities creating local certificates, and district courts ruling the absence unconstitutional.

laws.title: Specially Designated Secrets Act: Japan's Secrecy Law
laws.subtitle: Japan's 2013 secrecy law allows up to 10 years imprisonment for leaking vaguely-defined 'special secrets' — critics fear press freedom damage
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on the Protection of Specially Designated Secrets (2014) created a new category of classified information covering defense, diplomacy, counterterrorism, and counter-espionage. Government officials who leak designated secrets face up to 10 years imprisonment; journalists who solicit secrets face up to 5 years. Critics — including the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression — warned that the law's broad definition of 'secrets' and the absence of a public interest defense could criminalize investigative journalism. Japan has historically had a secretive relationship between government ministries and journalists through the 'kisha club' press club system.
laws.penalty: Leaking designated secrets: up to 10 years imprisonment. Soliciting or receiving secrets (journalists): up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: A parliamentary oversight committee was established to review designations
Information older than 60 years must be disclosed unless still classified under narrow exceptions
laws.sourceLabel: Cabinet Secretariat Japan – Specially Designated Secrets

quiz.q: How many years imprisonment can journalists face for soliciting 'specially designated secrets' under Japan's 2014 secrecy law?
quiz.explanation: Under Japan's Specially Designated Secrets Act, journalists who solicit or receive government secrets face up to 5 years imprisonment, while officials who leak them face up to 10 years — provisions that critics say chill investigative journalism.

laws.title: Japan's Historic Defense Buildup: Doubling Military Spending by 2027
laws.subtitle: Japan abandoned its post-WWII pacifist restraint by announcing the largest military expansion since 1945 — including counterstrike capabilities
laws.fullDescription: In December 2022, Japan's government under PM Kishida announced a fundamental shift in defense policy: Japan would double its defense spending from 1% to 2% of GDP by 2027 — the largest military buildup since WWII. Critically, Japan also announced it would acquire 'counterstrike capability' — the ability to strike enemy territory with long-range missiles — a dramatic departure from the exclusively defensive posture Japan had maintained since 1945. Japan's constitution (Article 9) formally renounces war and the maintenance of 'war potential.' The government interpreted counterstrike capability as defensive. The policy was driven by North Korea's missile tests, China's military expansion, and Russia's Ukraine invasion.
laws.penalty: Japan's Self-Defense Force operates under strict legal constraints. Overseas combat operations require specific Diet (parliamentary) authorization
exceptions: Article 9 reinterpretation: PM Abe in 2015 reinterpreted the constitution to allow 'collective self-defense' (helping allied nations under attack)
Counterstrike capability is classified as defensive rather than offensive to maintain constitutional compliance

quiz.q: What long-standing percentage cap on defense spending did Japan abandon when it announced doubling military expenditure?
quiz.explanation: Japan had maintained an informal 1% of GDP cap on defense spending since 1976 — reflecting its post-WWII pacifist restraint. The December 2022 announcement to double spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 was the most significant shift in Japanese defense policy since World War II.

laws.title: Article 9 War Renunciation
laws.subtitle: Japan's pacifist constitution bans the maintenance of war potential
laws.fullDescription: Article 9 of Japan's Constitution (1947), often called the 'Peace Constitution,' states that Japan 'forever renounces war as a sovereign right of the nation' and that 'land, sea, and air forces, as well as other war potential, will never be maintained.' Written during the US occupation, Article 9 has been the foundation of Japan's post-war pacifist identity. Japan's Self-Defense Forces technically comply through legal interpretation. In 2015, PM Abe reinterpreted the constitution to allow 'collective self-defense' — helping allies under attack. A full constitutional revision of Article 9 requires a two-thirds parliamentary vote plus national referendum.
laws.penalty: No individual criminal penalty — this is a constitutional provision; violations would be political/constitutional crises
exceptions: Japan maintains Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) under a reinterpretation that they are not 'war potential'
2015 reinterpretation allows collective self-defense operations with allies

quiz.q: What year was Japan's pacifist constitution, including Article 9, adopted?
quiz.explanation: Japan's post-war Constitution, drafted during the US occupation, came into force on May 3, 1947. Article 9's war renunciation clause was largely written to prevent Japan from rearming.

laws.title: National Holiday Law
laws.subtitle: Japan has 16 public holidays — the world's most — all defined by law
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on National Holidays (1948, amended multiple times) defines all public holidays by law. Japan has 16 official national holidays — the most of any country — including unique cultural observances: Respect for the Aged Day (third Monday of September), Sports Day (second Monday of October), Greenery Day (May 4), Marine Day (third Monday of July), and Mountain Day (August 11, added in 2016). When a holiday falls on Sunday, the following Monday becomes a substitute holiday. The 'Golden Week' (late April to early May) clusters four holidays into a ~10-day vacation season, causing Japan's busiest travel period.
laws.penalty: Employers who require workers to work on public holidays without compensation must pay holiday pay premium (125% of regular wage)
exceptions: Certain essential industries (healthcare, transportation, hospitality) operate on holidays with premium pay requirements
Self-employed individuals have no legal holiday entitlements

quiz.q: How many national public holidays does Japan have — the most of any country?
quiz.explanation: Japan has 16 official national public holidays defined by the Act on National Holidays — more than any other country. This includes unique observances like Respect for the Aged Day, Marine Day, and Mountain Day.

laws.title: My Number Social Security ID
laws.subtitle: Japan's 'My Number' system links taxes, pensions, and healthcare through a national ID
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Act on the Use of Numbers to Identify a Specific Individual in Administrative Procedures (My Number Act, 2013) established a national identification number for all Japanese residents — citizens and registered foreign residents — linking taxation, social security, and disaster management records. The 12-digit 'My Number' (マイナンバー) was rolled out from 2016. By 2023, My Number was being linked to health insurance cards (Mynaportal), driving licenses, and bank accounts. The system faced significant public resistance over privacy concerns and data breaches in 2023 — wrong numbers were linked to wrong accounts in thousands of cases, causing a political crisis.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent use of another person's My Number: criminal prosecution; unauthorized disclosure: up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: Temporary visitors on short-term visas do not receive My Numbers
Certain sensitive personal data cannot be stored in the My Number system by law

quiz.q: What is the Japanese term for the national ID number system established in 2013?
quiz.explanation: My Number (マイナンバー) is Japan's 12-digit national identification number system, linking tax, social security, and administrative records. Its 2023 expansion to health insurance cards triggered a political crisis after data linking errors affected thousands of people.

laws.title: Political Funds Control Act and 2023–2024 LDP Scandal
laws.subtitle: Japan's political funding law was at center of a major slush fund scandal that shook the ruling party
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Political Funds Control Act (政治資金規正法, Seiji Shikin Kisei Hō) governs how political parties and politicians raise and spend money. The 2023–2024 LDP (Liberal Democratic Party) political fund scandal revealed that factions within the LDP had systematically under-reported political fundraising income — collecting ticket money for fundraising parties and not entering the excess into official accounts, creating 'slush funds.' An estimated ¥600 million or more went unreported across multiple LDP factions over 5+ years. Multiple cabinet ministers resigned, the Abe and Nikai factions were dissolved, and Prime Minister Kishida's approval ratings hit historic lows before he resigned. The scandal led to amendments to the Political Funds Control Act in 2024, requiring broader disclosure of political donations including online fundraising. Japan's ruling LDP has governed for all but a few years since 1955.
laws.penalty: Undisclosed political donations: fines up to ¥1 million and/or 3 years imprisonment for responsible parties; political groups violating reporting: fines up to ¥500,000
exceptions: Small donations below ¥50,000 from individuals do not require full disclosure
Political party headquarters are subject to different reporting rules than individual politicians
Foreign donations are completely prohibited — no exception

laws.title: Declining Birth Rate Crisis and Immigration Policy Debate
laws.subtitle: Japan's record-low birth rate (1.2 in 2023) drives major legal debates on immigration and family policy
laws.fullDescription: Japan's total fertility rate fell to a record low of 1.2 in 2023 (down from 1.26 in 2022), far below the 2.1 replacement level. Japan's population has been declining since 2008 and is projected to fall from 125 million (2023) to under 90 million by 2060. This demographic crisis drives major policy debates with legal dimensions: the immigration reform debate (Japan enacted the revised Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act in 2023, expanding skilled worker visas and creating a new 'Specified Skilled Worker' status while maintaining strict limits on permanent settlement for lower-skill workers); the 'Idol Defense' discussion (whether Japan needs foreign workers to maintain defense industries); childcare policy (enhanced parental leave laws, the 2023 Child and Child-Rearing Support Act allocating ¥3.6 trillion for childcare); and joint custody reform (Japan enacted joint custody for divorced parents in 2024 after decades of single-custody only, completing a major family law overhaul).
laws.penalty: Overstay of visa: deportation and re-entry ban; violations of Specified Skilled Worker program conditions: visa revocation; failure to provide legally mandated parental leave: administrative sanctions
exceptions: Refugees recognized under the Refugee Recognition Act have permanent protection
Highly skilled foreign professionals under the points-based system have expedited permanent residence
Special permanent residents (primarily Korean-Japanese) have distinct status

laws.title: LDP Slush Fund Scandal and Political Fundraising Reform
laws.subtitle: Japan's ruling party was rocked by illegal political fundraising scandals in 2023-2024
laws.fullDescription: In 2023-2024, Japan's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) faced its worst political scandal in decades. Investigations revealed that LDP factions — particularly the Abe faction (Seiwa-kai) — had systematically underreported political fundraising party ticket sales, creating undisclosed slush funds totaling hundreds of millions of yen over years. Over 90 LDP members were implicated; dozens faced prosecution. Former PM Kishida dissolved the LDP's factions. The scandal contributed to Kishida's resignation and the LDP losing its parliamentary majority in October 2024 elections — its worst result since 2009. Reform to Japan's Political Funds Control Act was debated but critics said changes were insufficient.
laws.penalty: Political Funds Control Act violations: up to 3 years imprisonment and fines. Undisclosed donations: fines up to ¥500,000 and return of funds.
exceptions: Small party events and member contributions under threshold not subject to full disclosure
Donations to political parties (not individual politicians) have higher permitted limits
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications – Political Funds

quiz.q: What was the nature of Japan's 2023-2024 LDP political scandal?
options: LDP members were caught accepting bribes from defense contractors
LDP factions systematically underreported fundraising income, creating undisclosed slush funds
An LDP leader was found to have hidden bank accounts in Switzerland
LDP members illegally donated to foreign political campaigns
quiz.explanation: LDP factions — especially the Abe faction — systematically underreported fundraising ticket sales over years, creating slush funds totaling hundreds of millions of yen used outside normal political finance rules.

laws.title: Japan's Defense Budget Doubling and Security Policy Revolution
laws.subtitle: Japan committed to doubling its defense spending by 2027, ending its pacifist limitation
laws.fullDescription: Japan's 2022 National Security Strategy announced a historic shift: Japan would double its defense spending from roughly 1% of GDP to 2% by 2027 — becoming the world's third-largest defense spender. The policy reversal ended Japan's self-imposed post-WWII ceiling and was driven by threats from China (Taiwan), North Korean missiles, and Russia's Ukraine invasion. Japan also acquired counterstrike (enemy base attack) capability — previously considered offensive and thus unconstitutional under Article 9's pacifism. Tomahawk cruise missiles were purchased from the US. The government argued these were defensive preemptive strike capabilities, not offensive weapons. Opposition parties and constitutional scholars challenged the interpretation.
laws.penalty: Violations of arms export law: criminal prosecution. Defense procurement fraud: up to 10 years under anti-corruption law.
exceptions: Article 9 pacifism officially interpreted as permitting 'minimum necessary defense' including counterstrike capability
Weapons exports now permitted to countries in 'same values' group under revised defense export policy

quiz.q: What post-WWII limitation did Japan's 2022 National Security Strategy effectively end?
options: Japan's ban on hosting foreign military bases
Japan's self-imposed 1% GDP ceiling on defense spending, moving to 2%
Japan's ban on nuclear energy for defense purposes
Japan's constitutional prohibition on a standing army
quiz.explanation: Japan's 2022 security strategy committed to doubling defense spending from ~1% to 2% of GDP by 2027 — ending a decades-long self-imposed cap that reflected Japan's post-WWII pacifist commitments and making Japan one of the world's largest defense spenders.

laws.title: Japan's Revised Economic Security Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Protecting critical supply chains and sensitive technologies
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act (2022) established four pillars: strengthening critical supply chains (semiconductors, medical devices, rare earths), protecting critical infrastructure (electricity, gas, communications, transport), promoting sensitive technology research with government support, and restricting patents for sensitive inventions. Foreign investment in companies related to national security sectors requires prior government approval. The law reflects Japan's strategic response to supply chain vulnerabilities exposed by COVID-19 and US-China tech competition.
laws.penalty: Violating foreign investment screening requirements: orders to divest or modify investment. Non-compliance with divestment orders: criminal prosecution, up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥3 million fine. Unauthorized disclosure of designated sensitive patents: up to 2 years imprisonment
exceptions: Investments below threshold amounts exempt from prior screening
Portfolio investments without management control generally exempt
Pre-existing investments grandfather clause applies in some cases

quiz.q: What are the four pillars of Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act?
options: Supply chains, infrastructure, technology research, and sensitive patents
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act covers four pillars: critical supply chains, critical infrastructure protection, sensitive technology research promotion, and restriction of sensitive invention patents.

laws.title: Japan's LDP Funds Scandal and Political Reform
laws.subtitle: Secret political slush funds trigger biggest LDP crisis in decades
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) faced its worst political crisis in decades in 2023-2024 when it emerged that multiple LDP factions had systematically underreported political fundraising by failing to record income from fundraising parties — creating secret 'slush funds.' Over 100 LDP politicians were implicated. PM Kishida disbanded several LDP factions and pledged political funding reform. The Political Funds Control Act was amended to increase transparency. The scandal contributed to LDP losing its parliamentary majority in October 2024 elections, forcing Ishiba government to seek coalition partners.
laws.penalty: Violation of Political Funds Control Act: fines up to ¥500,000 and mandatory public disclosure. Systematic underreporting: up to 5 years imprisonment plus disqualification from public office. Bribery using slush funds: up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Political parties themselves have some exemptions from detailed reporting requirements
Small local chapters under ¥500,000 in annual revenue have simplified reporting
Internal party transfers between factions have some disclosure exemptions
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs - Political Funds

quiz.q: What political consequence did the LDP slush fund scandal have in Japan's October 2024 election?
quiz.explanation: Japan's LDP slush fund scandal — where over 100 politicians were implicated in underreporting fundraising — contributed to the LDP losing its parliamentary majority in the October 2024 elections for the first time in over a decade.

laws.title: Japan's Super-Aging Society Laws
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for world's oldest society addresses care and workforce needs
laws.fullDescription: Japan has the world's oldest population — 29% over 65 as of 2024 — and has enacted comprehensive legislation addressing super-aging. The Act on Comprehensively Advancing Long-Term Care Insurance expanded home care and community-based services. The Revised Health Insurance Act allows people to work and receive full pension past 65 (previously reduced). Japan raised the pensionable age incrementally to 65 and is considering further increases. The Revised Part-Time Labor Act improved working conditions for elderly part-time workers. Japan's care shortage is addressed by allowing more foreign care workers under the Technical Intern Training Program and Specified Skilled Worker programs.
laws.penalty: Long-term care fraud (false billing): criminal prosecution, up to 10 years. Elder abuse by care facility staff: up to 5 years. Violating elder care facility minimum staffing: license revocation. Age discrimination in hiring over 65: civil remedies under revised Employment Measures Act
exceptions: Mandatory retirement ages at 60 can be maintained under transitional provisions
Some public safety roles (police, firefighters) have mandatory retirement at lower ages
Religious and non-profit care providers have slightly different licensing requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare

quiz.q: What percentage of Japan's population is over 65 as of 2024?
quiz.explanation: Japan has 29% of its population over 65 as of 2024 — the world's highest proportion of elderly citizens — driving comprehensive legislative responses including expanded long-term care insurance, retirement age increases, and programs to bring in foreign care workers.

laws.title: Revised Fugitive Emissions and Carbon Neutrality Laws
laws.subtitle: Japan's GX Promotion Act creates a carbon market and green transition framework
laws.fullDescription: Japan's GX (Green Transformation) Promotion Act passed in 2023 establishes a framework for decarbonizing industry, including a carbon emissions trading system and green bonds. The Act requires large industrial emitters to participate in an emissions trading scheme phased in from 2026. Japan committed to carbon neutrality by 2050. The Act also provides subsidies for clean technology investment and nuclear energy expansion. Companies must disclose their transition plans. The GX Investment Strategy channels 150 trillion yen over 10 years into clean energy. Non-compliance with emissions reporting will face regulatory penalties.
laws.penalty: False emissions reporting: criminal fines; non-participation in mandatory ETS phases: administrative sanctions and public disclosure
exceptions: Small and medium enterprises excluded from mandatory ETS phases initially
Agriculture and forestry have separate carbon sink recognition frameworks
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

quiz.q: What does Japan's GX Promotion Act establish?
options: A carbon emissions trading system and green transition framework
quiz.explanation: Japan's GX (Green Transformation) Promotion Act of 2023 establishes a framework for industrial decarbonization, including a carbon emissions trading system and 150 trillion yen in clean energy investment over 10 years.

laws.title: Revised Economic Security Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Japan expanded its economic security law framework for critical technology protection
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act (2022) and its subsequent expansion created comprehensive requirements for protecting critical infrastructure, securing supply chains in specified sectors, developing sensitive technologies under government support, and restricting patents on technologies with national security implications. Companies in 14 critical infrastructure sectors must submit security plans. The Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office gained expanded oversight. Japan began limiting outbound investment in sensitive technology sectors. These laws significantly affect technology companies operating in Japan and Japanese companies investing abroad, particularly in semiconductor, AI, and quantum computing sectors.
laws.penalty: Non-compliance with critical infrastructure security plans: administrative orders and potential prosecution; patent restriction violations: criminal penalties
exceptions: Small companies under revenue thresholds in non-critical sectors
Research institutions under approved national security research frameworks

quiz.q: How many critical infrastructure sectors does Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act cover?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act covers 14 critical infrastructure sectors including electricity, gas, water, communications, financial systems, railroads, aviation, airports, ports, hospitals, water utilities, freight, aviation management systems, and credit cards.

laws.title: Security Three Documents and Defense Buildup Laws
laws.subtitle: Japan enacted a historic shift from pacifist defense posture under Kishida
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Kishida government approved three landmark security documents in December 2022: the National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program. These represented Japan's most significant security policy shift since WWII, doubling defense spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 and acquiring counterstrike (enemy base attack) capabilities. Legislation enabling these capabilities was enacted, including amendments to laws governing Japan's Self-Defense Forces. Article 9 of Japan's constitution (renouncing war) was reinterpreted rather than amended. Export controls on defense equipment were eased, allowing Japan to supply weapons to Ukraine for the first time.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized export of defense equipment: criminal prosecution under Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act
exceptions: Japan Ground Self-Defense Force exercises with US forces under Status of Forces Agreement
Defensive equipment transfers to specified countries under new transfer rules

quiz.q: What was significant about Japan's December 2022 National Security Strategy?
options: Japan doubled defense spending target and acquired counterstrike capabilities — a historic shift from pacifist posture
Japan ended its alliance with the US
quiz.explanation: Japan's December 2022 security documents were historically significant for doubling defense spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 and acquiring counterstrike capabilities against enemy bases — the most significant departure from Japan's post-WWII pacifist defense posture.

laws.title: Japan AI Strategy and Generative AI Guidelines
laws.subtitle: Japan takes a pro-innovation but safety-conscious approach to AI
laws.fullDescription: Japan has adopted a relatively permissive approach to AI regulation compared to the EU, favoring innovation while developing soft guidelines. The government published guidelines on generative AI for businesses emphasizing transparency, safety testing, and avoiding harmful uses. Japan also clarified that training AI on copyrighted material is generally permitted under Japanese copyright law for machine learning purposes, a more permissive stance than most countries. The government's AI Strategy focuses on using AI to address Japan's aging population challenges.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties under current AI guidelines; civil liability applies for AI-caused harm under general tort law
exceptions: Existing copyright and privacy law still applies
Medical AI under separate regulatory approval process
AI in financial services regulated by FSA
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

quiz.q: What copyright stance has Japan taken that is more permissive than most countries?
options: Banning all AI training on copyrighted material
Allowing AI training on copyrighted material for machine learning purposes
Requiring payment for all AI training data
Requiring government approval for AI training datasets
quiz.explanation: Japan clarified that training AI models on copyrighted material is generally permitted under Japanese copyright law for machine learning purposes, making it more permissive than the EU or US on this issue.

laws.title: Japan Revised Economic Security Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Japan protects critical technologies and supply chains from foreign acquisition
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act (2022) established frameworks for protecting critical infrastructure, ensuring stable supply chains for essential goods, promoting domestically developed technologies, and protecting sensitive patents. The law allows the government to screen and restrict foreign investment in critical sectors, require disclosures for AI and semiconductor technology transfers, and subsidize domestic production of critical components. It reflects Japan's response to US-China tech competition and supply chain vulnerabilities exposed by COVID-19.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized transfer of designated sensitive technologies: criminal penalties up to 2 years imprisonment and fines; foreign investment violations: orders and fines
exceptions: Academic research not involving classified technology
Small technology transfers below value thresholds
Allied country technology sharing under bilateral agreements

quiz.q: What supply chain vulnerability primarily motivated Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act?
options: Supply chain disruptions from COVID-19 and US-China tech competition
A major cyberattack on Japanese infrastructure
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act was partly motivated by supply chain vulnerabilities exposed by COVID-19 and by the escalating US-China technology competition affecting Japanese companies.

laws.title: Japan Revised Immigration Act — Deportation Reform
laws.subtitle: Japan strengthens deportation rules after controversy
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted a controversial revision to its Immigration Control Act in 2023, reducing protections against deportation for asylum seekers who apply repeatedly. Under the previous law, deportation was suspended for the duration of an asylum application, allowing indefinite repeated applications. The new law allows deportation to proceed after a third asylum application unless there are new grounds. Critics argued the change threatened genuine refugees, while the government argued it addressed abuse of the system.
laws.penalty: Overstay and unauthorized residence: deportation with potential multi-year ban on re-entry; filing false asylum claims: criminal penalties
exceptions: Genuine persecution risks are assessed in each case
Children born in Japan have special consideration
Medical emergencies prevent immediate deportation

quiz.q: What specific deportation protection did Japan's 2023 Immigration Act revision reduce?
options: Protection allowing repeated asylum applications to suspend deportation indefinitely
quiz.explanation: Japan's 2023 Immigration Act revision reduced the protection that had allowed repeated asylum applications to suspend deportation indefinitely — the new law allows deportation after a third application unless new grounds are presented.

laws.title: Active Senior Employment Promotion Law
laws.subtitle: Japan's legislation extending work opportunities for older citizens
laws.fullDescription: Japan's amended employment laws encourage and in some cases require companies to make efforts to ensure employment opportunities for workers up to age 70. Previously, the law required companies to employ workers until 65; the new provisions extend this with obligations to make reasonable efforts for workers aged 65-70 through re-employment, contract work, freelance arrangements, or social contribution activities. The reforms respond to Japan's severe demographic aging and labor shortage, and are part of a broader strategy to utilize senior workers.
laws.penalty: Companies that fail to make documented efforts for senior employment face administrative guidance; repeated non-compliance can result in public disclosure and fines
exceptions: Small businesses below 50 employees have simplified obligations
Creative and physically demanding roles have modified age-related provisions
Workers who voluntarily retire before 70 have no claim under the law
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Japan

quiz.q: Up to what age do Japanese employment laws now require companies to make efforts to provide employment opportunities?
quiz.explanation: Japan's amended employment law extends company obligations to make employment opportunity efforts for workers up to age 70, responding to the country's severe demographic aging and labor shortage.

laws.title: Economic Security Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Japan's law protecting critical technologies and supply chains
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act established a legal framework for protecting critical technologies, supply chains, critical infrastructure, and advanced patents from foreign exploitation. The law requires vulnerability assessments for 14 critical industries, mandates government review of technology transfers and investments in sensitive sectors, creates a classified patent system for inventions with national security implications, and provides economic support for domestic production of critical components. The law reflects Japan's response to dependence on foreign suppliers for semiconductors and other strategic goods.
laws.penalty: Violations of supply chain security requirements carry fines and potentially revocation of operating licenses for critical infrastructure; illegal technology transfers to prohibited parties carry criminal charges
exceptions: Academic research collaborations have modified review procedures
Allied nation technology transfers have expedited review
Consumer technology not involving critical sectors is exempt

quiz.q: How many critical industries does Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act require to conduct vulnerability assessments?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act identifies 14 critical industries required to conduct vulnerability assessments and improve supply chain resilience, covering sectors from semiconductors and electric vehicles to pharmaceuticals and aviation.

laws.title: Defense Industry Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Japan's legislation supporting domestic weapons production for export
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted laws allowing the export of weapons and defense equipment, a significant departure from its post-war peace constitution traditions. The government revised its Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment, relaxed rules on exporting co-developed weapons systems, and created legal frameworks for government-to-government defense equipment sales. Japan agreed to supply Patriot missiles to the United States and co-develops fighters with the UK and Italy. Domestic defense industry companies were given government support to expand capacity. The changes reflect Japan's broader rearmament under the 2023 National Defense Strategy.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized export of controlled defense items carries criminal prosecution under export control law; deception in export license applications carries criminal charges
exceptions: Civilian technologies with dual-use applications follow separate export control rules
Research and development exports to allied nations have expedited approval pathways
Historical military equipment transfers to museums are not covered by new restrictions

quiz.q: What did Japan's revised Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment allow for the first time?
options: Conscription of citizens for the military
Export of Japanese-made weapons and defense equipment
quiz.explanation: Japan's revised Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment significantly relaxed post-war restrictions to allow export of Japanese weapons and defense equipment, representing a historic departure from the pacifist interpretation of Japan's constitution that had restricted defense exports.

laws.title: Japan Children's Future Strategy and Childcare Leave Reforms
laws.subtitle: Expanded paternity leave and childcare subsidies to reverse declining birthrate
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted the Children's Future Strategy in 2023, a comprehensive policy package to address the country's record-low birthrate (1.20 in 2023). Key measures include expanding childcare leave pay to 80% of salary (up from 67%), making childcare free for third and subsequent children, increasing child allowances to age 18, and creating a new children's agency (Kodomo-Cho) with a dedicated budget. The strategy aims to double child-related spending as a share of GDP.
laws.penalty: Employers who obstruct eligible employees from taking childcare leave face fines of up to ¥500,000 under the Child Care and Family Care Leave Law. Repeat violations subject to public disclosure of company name.
exceptions: Self-employed workers not covered by employment insurance access separate grant programs
Fixed-term contract workers meeting tenure requirements gain access to childcare leave benefits
Small businesses under 100 employees have extended implementation timelines for some provisions

quiz.q: What was Japan's total fertility rate in 2023, prompting the Children's Future Strategy?
quiz.explanation: Japan recorded a total fertility rate of 1.20 in 2023, a historic low, which was a primary driver for enacting the comprehensive Children's Future Strategy with expanded childcare leave and subsidies.

laws.title: Japan Economic Security Promotion Act
laws.subtitle: Protecting critical supply chains and infrastructure from foreign threats
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act (2022, implemented through 2023–2024) established four pillars: securing supply chains for critical goods (semiconductors, rare earths, medical supplies), protecting critical infrastructure (14 sectors including energy, finance, water, communications) from sabotage or cyberattack, supporting basic technology research, and creating a patent non-disclosure system for sensitive technologies. The law required companies to submit supply chain security plans and allowed government audits of critical infrastructure.
laws.penalty: Companies that fail to submit required supply chain security plans: administrative fines of JPY 1 million. Unauthorized disclosure of classified sensitive technologies under the non-disclosure system: criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 2 years.
exceptions: Small and medium enterprises in critical sectors with turnover under JPY 5 billion have extended compliance timelines
Academic research institutions publishing in peer-reviewed journals not subject to non-disclosure provisions except for national security-classified topics
Technologies already publicly available internationally exempt from domestic non-disclosure requirements

quiz.q: How many critical infrastructure sectors are protected under Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act designates 14 critical infrastructure sectors (including energy, finance, water, communications, airports, railways, and others) for protection against sabotage, cyberattack, and foreign interference — a significant expansion of Japan's national security framework.

laws.title: Japan Active Aging Society Law
laws.subtitle: Extending retirement, expanding senior employment opportunities
laws.fullDescription: Japan, with the world's oldest population (median age approximately 48), enacted legislation in 2023–2024 expanding programs to keep seniors employed and socially active. The law encouraged companies to extend employment options to age 70 (up from mandatory retirement at 60 and a previous target of 65), provided tax incentives for employers who create senior-friendly workplaces, expanded 'social participation activities' for retired persons, and reformed pension rules to allow flexible part-time work without pension reduction.
laws.penalty: Age discrimination in employment against workers aged 60–70 who wish to continue working: civil liability under the Age Discrimination in Employment Law, compensatory damages up to 12 months salary.
exceptions: Physical or safety-based job requirements that cannot be accommodated for older workers may justify non-extension in those specific roles
Jobs requiring aviation or nuclear safety certifications with age limits set by safety regulations not subject to general extension principles

quiz.q: To what age did Japan's 2023-2024 legislation encourage companies to extend employment options?
quiz.explanation: Japan's active aging legislation encouraged companies to extend employment options to age 70, up from mandatory retirement typically at 60 and previous government targets of 65. With Japan's extreme demographic aging, extending working lives is seen as essential to maintaining economic productivity.

laws.title: Equal Pay for Equal Work (Hatarakikata Kaikaku)
laws.subtitle: Japan's work style reform laws requiring pay parity for contract workers
laws.fullDescription: Japan's Work Style Reform laws took full effect, requiring companies to provide equal pay for equal work between regular and non-regular employees (part-time, fixed-term, dispatched workers). Companies must disclose pay gap data between regular and irregular workers and justify any differences. The laws also capped overtime hours at 100/month (960/year) across all industries including previously exempt sectors.
laws.penalty: Violations of overtime caps: fines up to ¥300,000 per worker per month; unequal pay without justification: labour tribunal orders to pay back wages
exceptions: Senior management and certain professional tracks negotiated separately
Construction and driver industries have modified overtime caps transitioning to full limits
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Japan

quiz.q: What is Japan's annual overtime cap per worker under the Work Style Reform laws?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Work Style Reform laws cap overtime at 960 hours per year (100 hours per month) for most workers, with criminal penalties for employers who exceed these limits.

laws.title: Children's Future Strategy and Pronatalist Emergency Measures
laws.subtitle: Japan doubles child allowances and creates childcare entitlements
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted the Children's Future Strategy, doubling child allowances, extending them to ages up to 18, creating an entitlement to childcare centre placement, expanding parental leave rights, and introducing a new childcare levy on companies. The strategy responded to Japan's fertility rate falling to a record low of 1.20 in 2023. The measures were funded by a new social insurance levy.
laws.penalty: Employers not granting statutory childcare leave: fines of up to ¥500,000; companies not meeting childcare levy obligations: administrative penalties
exceptions: Small businesses under 100 employees given phased implementation for new levy
Government workers covered under separate civil service family support regulations

quiz.q: What was Japan's record-low fertility rate in 2023 that prompted emergency pronatalist measures?
quiz.explanation: Japan's total fertility rate fell to a record low of 1.20 in 2023, far below the 2.1 replacement rate, prompting the government to declare a demographic emergency and enact its Children's Future Strategy.

laws.title: Nuclear Restart Programme and Long-Life Extension
laws.subtitle: Japan restarts more nuclear plants after decade of post-Fukushima shutdowns
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted legislation accelerating the restart of nuclear plants that had been offline since Fukushima and creating a 60-year (extendable to 80-year) maximum operational life for nuclear reactors, replacing the earlier 40-year rule. New safety review standards required earthquake and tsunami protection upgrades. By 2024, Japan had restarted 12 reactors and planned for more.
laws.penalty: Nuclear operators failing safety review conditions: mandatory shutdown; improper safety data reporting: criminal prosecution of executives
exceptions: Research reactors at universities continue under separate NRA oversight
Prototype fast breeder reactor Monju subject to separate decommissioning schedule
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry Japan

quiz.q: What maximum operational age for nuclear reactors did Japan's new law allow?
quiz.explanation: Japan replaced its earlier 40-year operational limit with a new framework allowing reactors to operate up to 60 years, with the possibility of extension to 80 years following additional safety inspections — a major policy shift from the post-Fukushima conservative approach.

laws.title: Japan AI Safety Institute and Hiroshima AI Process
laws.subtitle: Japan leads international AI governance through G7
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted legislation establishing the Japan AI Safety Institute (AISI) on a statutory basis, following its leadership of the G7 Hiroshima AI Process. The law required AI developers to conduct risk assessments, submit to government AI evaluations for high-risk systems, and contribute to developing international AI safety standards. Japan's approach balanced innovation with safety without prescriptive product bans.
laws.penalty: AI developers that misrepresent safety assessments: fines and mandatory re-evaluation; high-risk AI systems deployed without assessment: suspension order
exceptions: Research AI systems in university settings exempt from commercial safety assessment requirements
Legacy AI systems in operation before the law's enactment receive 2-year grandfathering

quiz.q: What international AI governance process did Japan lead through the G7?
quiz.explanation: The Hiroshima AI Process was an international AI governance framework launched at the G7 Hiroshima Summit in 2023 under Japan's presidency, producing voluntary codes of conduct for advanced AI developers that influenced subsequent national regulations globally.

laws.title: Japan Robot and AI Workforce Integration Act
laws.subtitle: Managing automation transition in aging society
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted the Robot and AI Workforce Integration and Economic Revitalization Act 2025, addressing both the labour shortages from Japan's demographic crisis and the transformation of work through automation. The law mandates 'Robot Readiness Assessments' for all companies with over 100 employees identifying automation potential, provides ¥5 trillion in tax credits for SMEs adopting industrial robots and AI systems, establishes Robot Safety Standards through METI with liability frameworks for robot-caused workplace injuries, creates a Universal Reskilling Fund funded by automation productivity gains providing ¥500,000 per worker for career transition support, and introduces the Japan Digital Artisan Programme preserving traditional craft skills through AI-assisted apprenticeship documentation.
laws.penalty: Robot safety standard non-compliance causing injury: ¥50 million plus criminal prosecution; automation tax credit fraud: ¥200 million plus 15 years; Universal Reskilling Fund misuse: ¥100 million plus imprisonment
exceptions: Companies under 50 employees have 3-year extended timeline for Robot Readiness Assessment
Agricultural robotics follow simplified safety standards for outdoor environments
Defense robotics governed under Ministry of Defense framework

quiz.q: How much per worker does Japan's Universal Reskilling Fund provide for career transition support funded by automation productivity gains?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Universal Reskilling Fund, funded by automation productivity gains under the Robot and AI Workforce Integration Act, provides ¥500,000 per worker to support career transitions as automation displaces traditional job roles.

laws.title: Japan Political Reform and Black Money Scandal Response
laws.subtitle: LDP reform after political funding scandal
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted the Political Ethics and Funding Transparency Act 2025, responding to the major 'Uragane' (black money) political funding scandal in which dozens of LDP politicians had failed to report political event ticket proceeds as political donations, triggering the fall of the Kishida government and significant LDP losses in the October 2024 elections. The law mandates real-time online disclosure of all political donations above ¥50,000 (reduced from ¥200,000), prohibits political fundraising events organized by factional groupings (imploding the LDP's faction system), creates the Political Finance Audit Commission as independent oversight body, introduces criminal penalties for politicians who knowingly fail to report political income, and establishes a whistleblower protection framework for political staff who report irregularities.
laws.penalty: Political funding non-disclosure above threshold: 5 years imprisonment plus ¥50 million fine; political faction fundraising in prohibited form: ¥100 million plus dissolution order; Political Finance Audit Commission obstruction: 10 years
exceptions: Political parties' headquarters operations retained under simplified disclosure (not faction-level)
Online crowdfunding for election campaigns has modified real-time disclosure framework
International political donations already prohibited and governed under separate framework

quiz.q: What was the Japanese term for the political funding scandal that triggered LDP losses in 2024 and led to the 2025 Political Ethics Act?
quiz.explanation: 'Uragane' (裏金, 'black money') was the term for the scandal in which dozens of LDP politicians had failed to declare proceeds from political fundraising events as income — a systematic accounting fraud that triggered significant LDP election losses and prompted the 2025 Political Ethics Act.

laws.title: LDP Political Funds Scandal Reform and Election Law Act
laws.subtitle: Campaign finance transparency after slush fund revelations
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted sweeping political finance reform legislation following revelations that Liberal Democratic Party factions had operated illegal slush funds by underreporting fundraising dinner proceeds over many years. The law mandates full digital disclosure of political donations and expenditures, abolishes the 'party ticket' fundraising system, imposes criminal penalties on politicians who conceal funds, and establishes an independent oversight body for political finance audits.
laws.penalty: Politicians who conceal political funds face up to five years imprisonment and permanent disqualification from public office. Political parties that fail to comply with disclosure requirements face dissolution of their funding status.
exceptions: Small donations under 50,000 yen from individuals do not require individual donor disclosure
Legacy provisions allow previously undisclosed historical donations to be amnestied if voluntarily reported within one year

quiz.q: What practice was at the center of Japan's LDP political funds scandal?
options: Underreporting fundraising dinner proceeds to create slush funds
Using public funds for party events
quiz.explanation: LDP factions were found to have systematically underreported proceeds from 'party ticket' fundraising dinners, creating hidden slush funds over many years.

laws.title: Economic Security and Semiconductor Reindustrialization Act
laws.subtitle: Bringing advanced chip production back to Japan
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted economic security legislation aimed at reviving its semiconductor industry, which had declined significantly from its 1990s dominance. The law provides major subsidies for TSMC's Kumamoto facility and a new 2nm chip facility, creates a national semiconductor research program, establishes strategic stockpile requirements for critical minerals, and restricts Chinese investment in sensitive Japanese technology companies.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized transfer of designated sensitive technology to foreign entities without government approval carries up to 5 years imprisonment. Companies that fail strategic stockpile requirements face loss of government contracts.
exceptions: Established Japanese-Western joint ventures in non-sensitive technology sectors retain streamlined investment review
Academic technology exchanges with approved partner universities are exempt from transfer restrictions

quiz.q: Which Taiwanese company built a major new semiconductor facility in Japan's Kumamoto prefecture?
quiz.explanation: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company), the world's leading contract chipmaker, built a major new fabrication facility in Kumamoto, Japan — a landmark in Japan's effort to revive domestic semiconductor production.

laws.title: LDP Reform and Political Finance Cleanup Act
laws.subtitle: Electoral transparency after slush fund scandal
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted landmark political finance reform legislation following the LDP slush fund scandal that revealed systematic underreporting of fundraising income by party factions. The law abolishes the 'party ticket' (seiwankai) fundraising system, mandates full digital disclosure of all political donations above 50,000 yen, creates an independent Political Finance Commission, imposes criminal penalties on politicians who conceal funds, and dissolves the LDP factions that had maintained the slush funds.
laws.penalty: Politicians who fail to disclose political funds face up to five years imprisonment and permanent disqualification from elected office. Party officials who maintain hidden fund accounts face up to seven years.
exceptions: Grassroots fundraising events with donations under 50,000 yen per donor do not require individual donor disclosure
New political parties formed after the reform have a one-year grace period for full compliance system implementation

quiz.q: What LDP internal structures were dissolved as part of Japan's political finance reform?
quiz.explanation: Japan's political finance reform led to the formal dissolution of LDP factions (habatsu) — informal internal party groupings that had organized fundraising and power within the party for decades, and through which the slush fund system operated.

laws.title: Overtourism Management and Fuji-san Protection Act
laws.subtitle: Managing mass tourism damage to iconic sites
laws.fullDescription: Japan enacted tourism management legislation following the explosion of inbound tourism that created overcrowding at Kyoto, Mount Fuji, and other iconic destinations. The law authorizes municipalities to charge tourist taxes, limits daily climbers on Mount Fuji's Yoshida trail, creates 'no photography' zones in Kyoto's geisha districts that had been overwhelmed, mandates overtourism management plans for destinations receiving over 1 million visitors annually, and creates cultural sensitivity education for tour operators.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized climbing on closed Fuji trails carries fines up to ¥200,000. Photography in restricted Kyoto districts carries fines up to ¥10,000. Tour operators who violate cultural sensitivity requirements face license suspension.
exceptions: Japanese citizens have reduced restrictions on Fuji climbing compared to international tourists
Scientific and research expeditions retain access to restricted areas with special permits

quiz.q: What controversial measure did the Fujikawaguchiko town implement to deter Fuji overcrowding that sparked global attention?
options: Installing a physical barrier blocking the popular 'Lawson convenience store' Fuji photo spot
Closing Mount Fuji entirely to tourists
Requiring a lottery system for all visitors
quiz.explanation: Fujikawaguchiko town installed a large black barrier blocking the now-famous view of Mount Fuji from a Lawson convenience store parking lot — a spot that had gone viral on social media and attracted massive crowds creating traffic chaos. The dramatic measure drew global media attention to Japan's overtourism problems.

laws.title: Japan Defense Industry Development and Export Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Arms Export Restriction Relaxation Law
laws.fullDescription: Significantly relaxes Japan's post-WWII restrictions on arms exports, allowing Japan to export defense equipment to allied nations for the first time. The law permits exports of Japan-developed F-X fighter jets to third countries, allows sale of missile defense components to US allies, establishes security framework agreements with partner nations, and creates export control mechanisms. The reform represents Japan's most significant shift in security policy in decades.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for unauthorized arms exports; fines up to ¥500 million for export control violations
exceptions: Countries under arms embargoes cannot receive Japanese defense exports
Purely defensive systems exported before offensive capabilities

quiz.q: What does Japan's Defense Export Reform Act allow for the first time?
options: Export of defense equipment to allied nations
quiz.explanation: Japan's act allows export of defense equipment to allied nations for the first time, relaxing post-WWII restrictions.

laws.title: Japan Economic Security Promotion Act for Semiconductors
laws.subtitle: Critical Technology Supply Chain Protection Law
laws.fullDescription: Strengthens Japan's economic security framework for semiconductor and advanced technology supply chains. The law mandates domestic production capacity for critical chips, creates the Japan Chips Fund for semiconductor investment, restricts foreign acquisitions of Japanese semiconductor companies, establishes export controls for advanced manufacturing technology, and creates a strategic stockpile of critical minerals and chip components.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for unauthorized technology transfers; fines up to ¥1 billion for supply chain security violations
exceptions: Allied nation companies with security agreements receive preferential access
Legacy chip manufacturing (28nm+) has relaxed controls
laws.sourceLabel: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

quiz.q: What financial vehicle does Japan's Economic Security Act create for chip investment?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act creates the Japan Chips Fund to support domestic semiconductor investment and production capacity.

laws.title: Japan Political Funds Reform and LDP Scandal Response Act
laws.subtitle: Money in Politics and Donation Transparency Law
laws.fullDescription: Reforms political fund management following the LDP slush fund scandal that damaged PM Kishida's government. The law mandates public disclosure of political donation income, eliminates the political funds party account (seiji shikin kikin kanri dantai) that allowed opaque transfers, creates criminal penalties for unreported political funds, establishes independent auditing of party finances, and creates the Political Ethics Commission with investigative powers.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution and up to 5 years imprisonment for political funds violations; party fund suspension
exceptions: Small grassroots donations under 50,000 yen have simplified reporting
Local municipal party chapters have phased implementation

quiz.q: What LDP scandal drove Japan's Political Funds Reform Act?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Political Funds Reform Act was driven by the LDP slush fund scandal involving unreported political donations that damaged PM Kishida's government.

laws.title: Japan Ishiba Government Coalition Minority and Budget Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Post-Election Minority Government Fiscal Management Law
laws.fullDescription: Establishes governance frameworks for PM Ishiba's LDP-Komeito minority government following the 2024 election where the coalition lost its majority. The law creates cross-party budget negotiation frameworks, establishes the LDP's cooperation mechanisms with Nippon Ishin and DPP, implements the economic rescue package for cost-of-living crisis, and creates mechanisms for passing legislation without a majority.
laws.penalty: No-confidence motion procedures for budget failures; snap election triggers
exceptions: National security decisions maintain strong executive authority
Foreign policy decisions require cabinet rather than full parliamentary approval

quiz.q: What happened to Japan's LDP-Komeito coalition in the 2024 election?
quiz.explanation: Japan's LDP-Komeito coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the 2024 election, forcing PM Ishiba to govern as a minority with cross-party cooperation.

laws.title: Yen Depreciation Crisis and BOJ Policy Shift
laws.subtitle: Bank of Japan Raises Rates After Decades of Ultra-Low Policy
